**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Synchronize loan amount fields with account currency**

In the manual create/edit form, selecting a different `account[currency]` only triggers the balance field's `money-field` controller in `app/views/accounts/_form.html.erb`; these nested fields are now rendered once from the old `account.currency` and have no select/action through which to receive the change. Their symbol, separator, and step therefore stay at the family/previous currency, and `money_field_controller#canonicalizeForSubmit` rounds using that stale step (for example, creating a USD-family loan in KWD turns `1.234` into `1.23` while the account is saved as KWD). Propagate the account currency change to both hidden-currency fields.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the insurance comment to its test**

Adding the currency test here leaves the existing blank-option/check-constraint comment separated from `the insurance type's blank option clears a recorded type`, so it now appears to introduce an unrelated currency test. Move this new block above that comment or move the comment down with the insurance test so the documented intent remains attached to the current behavior.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L10-L10](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/6de7d32b18c759900afc1bc42756643a43e9945f/AGENTS.md#L10-L10)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the old picker history from the test comment**

The sentence about the picker being submitted/dropped and the form reverting documents the implementation history of this fix rather than a current invariant exercised by the test. Keep the useful statement that loan amounts use the account currency, but leave the old failure narrative in the commit/PR description so this comment does not age with the implementation.

Full details: Linked Issues check
**Explanation** Issue `#4529` requires that "Initial balance" and "Down payment" show the loan account's currency. It also allows either persisting a chosen currency or not offering the choice. The head implements the second option. In app/views/loans/_form.html.erb, both money_field calls now pass currency_value_override: account.currency and hide_currency: true (replacing default_currency: Current.family.currency). In app/views/shared/_money_field.html.erb, currency_value_override sets the symbol and the currency used for formatting. hide_currency suppresses the currency select, so no unpersisted choice is offered. The new form is rendered from loans/new.html.erb with account: `@account`, so account is defined on both new and edit. LoansController permits no accountable currency attribute, which matches the removed picker. The new test in test/controllers/loans_controller_test.rb (EUR account, edit form) asserts there is no accountable_attributes[currency] select and that the € symbol appears inside each amount's money-field for initial_balance and down_payment. This covers the coding requirement. The author reports the test fails on main and passes with the change. I did not run the test suite. The claim that Loan#original_balance reads amounts in the account currency comes from the PR description and was not independently verified in the model code.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check
**Explanation** The whole-PR diff against the merge base changes two files. app/views/loans/_form.html.erb removes the family-currency default and the currency picker for the two loan amount fields, which is the issue's scope. The added comment in that file explains the reason for the change. test/controllers/loans_controller_test.rb gains one test that covers this behavior. No unrelated code, configuration, or dependency changes appear in the summary or the inspected diffs. One minor issue: the new test is inserted between the existing comment block about the insurance rate type and the test that comment describes ("the insurance type's blank option clears a recorded type"). That comment now appears to describe the new test. This is a readability defect in the test file, not an unrelated change.
